mainTopic: Bread baked with forbidden or הקדש wood, and רבי יהודה's proofs that חמץ must be burned
overview: The גמרא infers that the רבנן permit bread baked with ערלה wood even when the flame was right next to the bread. It then asks when such wood is ever forbidden for them, and answers: when one uses the wood itself, such as a stool. רמי בר חמא asks רב חסדא about bread baked with הקדש wood, and רב חסדא forbids it. רבא explains why this differs from ערלה: הקדש is never nullified. רבא then raises a stronger difficulty. The person who heated the oven committed מעילה, which should make the wood חולין. רב פפא answers that the case is שלמים wood, following רבי יהודה, so the wood stays holy. The גמרא also challenges the idea that מעילה makes הקדש into חולין, using a ברייתא about holy ash. רמי בר חמא and רב שמעיה each answer that challenge. Finally the גמרא turns to רבי יהודה's view in the משנה that חמץ must be burned. It follows his proofs from נותר and the חכמים' counter-examples, and this debate continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Inference: the רבנן permit even when the flame faces the bread
steps.stepSummary: From the limit placed on רבי's prohibition, the גמרא infers that the רבנן permit the bread even when the flame was opposite it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this show that the רבנן, who disagree with him, permit the bread even when the flame is opposite it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion about the רבנן's view from the earlier statement that רבי forbids the bread only when the flame faced it. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that רבי forbids the bread only when the burning wood faced the bread directly. If so, the רבנן's argument must be about exactly that case, so they permit even then. This makes the רבנן very lenient, and the next step tests whether that is reasonable.

keyTerms.meaning: The flame is opposite it, burning right next to the bread

phrases.english: Does this imply that the Rabbis who disagree with him
permit even when the flame is opposite it?
phrases.notes: Even when the forbidden wood's fire directly bakes the bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues earlier's limit on רבי's prohibition (only when the flame is opposite the bread).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the רבנן permit the bread even in the strongest case, where the flame faced the bread.

steps.title: When would wood ever be forbidden for the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: If the רבנן permit even when the flame faces the bread, when is forbidden wood ever forbidden according to them?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, according to the רבנן, where do you find forbidden wood actually being forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference. If the רבנן permit even this direct benefit, it seems the wood's prohibition would never matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ערלה wood is אסור בהנאה, forbidden for any benefit. If baking with its direct flame is allowed, it is unclear what benefit the prohibition still blocks. The question is: what is left of the prohibition according to the רבנן?

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden wood, such as ערלה wood
How would you find them? In what case does this apply?

phrases.english: But forbidden wood, according to the Rabbis,
in what case do you find it forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא עֵצִים דְּאִיסּוּרָא לְרַבָּנַן הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion drawn in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that the רבנן permit the bread even when the flame is opposite it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even the most direct use of the fire is permitted, the prohibition on benefiting from the wood seems to have no practical effect.

steps.title: Using the wood itself, such as a stool
steps.stepSummary: רב אמי בר חמא answers that the prohibition applies when one benefits from the wood itself, for example a stool made from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אמי בר חמא said: in the case of a stool.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אמי בר חמא shows a case where even the רבנן forbid the wood. If you make a stool from it and sit on it, that is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן permit only benefit that comes indirectly from the burning wood, through the bread. Direct use of the wood as an object, like sitting on a stool made from it, stays fully forbidden. So the prohibition still has real force.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן, bread baked with forbidden wood is permitted, even with the flame opposite it. But direct use of the wood itself, like a stool, is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Ami bar Ḥama said:
In the case of a stool.
phrases.notes: Benefit from the wood itself, not from its fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a case where the prohibition still applies
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the רבנן permit bread baked with the flame opposite it, the wood's prohibition might seem meaningless.
steps.terutzMaskana: Direct use of the wood, such as a stool, is forbidden even according to the רבנן.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא asks about an oven heated with הקדש wood
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks רב חסדא: according to the lenient רבנן, is bread baked with הקדש wood permitted?
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked רב חסדא: an oven heated with הקדש wood, and bread was baked in it. According to the רבנן, who permitted in the first case, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רמי בר חמא asks whether the רבנן's leniency for ערלה wood also applies to הקדש wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן permitted bread baked with ערלה wood. The question is whether הקדש, holy property belonging to the בית המקדש, follows the same rule or is stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated wood belonging to the Temple
In the first case (the ערלה case)

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama asked Rav Ḥisda:
An oven that one heated with consecrated wood,
and he baked bread in it,
according to the Rabbis who permitted in the first case, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new inquiry that extends the רבנן's leniency to a different kind of forbidden wood.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether bread baked with הקדש wood is permitted according to the רבנן.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the bread is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that bread baked with הקדש wood is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: the bread is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers that, unlike with ערלה, this bread is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא treats הקדש more strictly than ערלה, even according to the lenient רבנן. He does not yet give a reason, which leads to the next challenge.

phrases.english: He said to him: The bread is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Bread baked with הקדש wood is forbidden.

steps.title: How is this different from ערלה?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא objects: why should הקדש be different from ערלה, where the bread is permitted?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between this and ערלה?!
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא challenges רב חסדא's answer by comparing it to the ערלה case, where the רבנן permit the bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ערלה and הקדש are forbidden for benefit, and in both cases the bread was baked with that wood. So it seems they should have the same law.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit (and its peels) from a tree's first three years, forbidden for benefit

phrases.english: What is the difference between this and orla?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's ruling in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that bread baked with הקדש wood is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ערלה and הקדש are both forbidden for benefit, so they should be treated alike, and ערלה bread is permitted.

steps.title: רבא rejects the comparison: הקדש is never nullified
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the comparison is no good. ערלה is nullified in 200 parts, but הקדש is not nullified even in 1,000.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: How can you compare them? ערלה is nullified in two hundred, but הקדש is not nullified even in a thousand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends רב חסדא by showing that ערלה and הקדש are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ערלה becomes בטל, nullified, when mixed one part in 200, so the tiny effect of the wood in the bread can be ignored. הקדש is never nullified, not even one part in 1,000. So the smallest trace of it still forbids the bread.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (rejecting a comparison)

phrases.english: Rava said: How can these be compared?!
Orla is nullified in two hundred,
consecrated property is not nullified even in a thousand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between ערלה and הקדש.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rules of nullification differ. ערלה can be nullified, but הקדש never can, so the bread's tiny trace of הקדש still forbids it.

steps.title: רבא's real difficulty: מעילה turns the wood into חולין
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the better question is this: whoever heated the oven committed מעילה, and מעילה makes the wood חולין, so the bread should be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: If there is a difficulty, this is it. Didn't the one who heated the oven commit מעילה? And wherever the one heating commits מעילה, the wood becomes חולין!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא replaces רמי בר חמא's weak question with a stronger one against רב חסדא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When someone uses הקדש for himself by mistake, he commits מעילה. The object then loses its holiness and becomes חולין, and he must pay back the בית המקדש. So by the time the fire baked the bread, the wood was already ordinary, and the bread should be permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: He committed מעילה, misuse of הקדש

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing that הקדש can be nullified. He accepts that it cannot. His point is that the wood may have stopped being הקדש altogether, through מעילה, before the bread was baked.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
If he found it difficult, this is the difficulty:
Didn't the one who heated it commit misuse of consecrated property?
And anywhere that the heater commits misuse,
the wood goes out to non-sacred status!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: אִי קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ — הָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the ערלה comparison, רבא offers a stronger challenge to step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that the bread is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מעילה removes the wood's holiness, so the bread was baked with חולין wood and should be permitted.

steps.title: רב פפא: שלמים wood, following רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the case is wood of שלמים, and the ruling follows רבי יהודה, who holds that הקדש loses its holiness only when misused unintentionally.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Here we are dealing with wood of שלמים, according to רבי יהודה, who said: הקדש used unintentionally becomes desecrated; used intentionally, it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers רבא's difficulty by defining the case so that the wood never lost its holiness. This keeps the bread forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wood of שלמים, which are קדשים קלים, is not subject to the normal laws of מעילה, so using it does not automatically make it חולין. According to רבי יהודה, holy property becomes desecrated only through unintentional מעילה; any other use leaves it holy. So the wood stayed הקדש, and since הקדש is never nullified, the bread is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Becomes desecrated, loses its holy status

steps.whatToRemember: Bread baked with הקדש wood is forbidden because הקדש is never nullified. This holds when the wood kept its holiness: wood of שלמים, following רבי יהודה, under whom only unintentional מעילה removes holiness.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step shows that the bread's status depends on whether the wood was still holy at the moment of baking. That turns on the rules of מעילה and desecration.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Here we are dealing with wood of peace-offerings,
and according to Rabbi Yehuda, who said:
consecrated property used unintentionally becomes desecrated;
used intentionally, it does not become desecrated.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הָכָא בַּעֲצֵי שְׁלָמִים עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's difficulty in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case to a specific type of wood and a specific opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Heating the oven was מעילה, so the wood became חולין and the bread should be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wood was שלמים wood, which is not subject to standard מעילה. Following רבי יהודה, it stayed holy, so the bread is forbidden.

steps.title: Why intentional misuse and שלמים wood never become חולין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבי יהודה's view. Only something that can carry a מעילה penalty can leave its holiness. שלמים wood cannot carry that penalty, so it stays forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does using it on purpose not take it out of holiness? Because a person who does it on purpose is not in the category of מעילה, so the object does not become חולין. The same is true for שלמים. Since they are not in the category of מעילה, the wood does not become חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב פפא's answer by explaining the reasoning behind רבי יהודה's rule and applying it to שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי יהודה, הקדש becomes חולין only through an act that counts as real מעילה. Real מעילה is done by accident (שוגג). Doing it on purpose does not count, so the object stays holy. שלמים (before the blood is sprinkled) are also not subject to מעילה at all. So even accidental use does not free the wood, and the bread stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Subject to the laws of מעילה (misusing holy property)

steps.whyThisMatters: This removes רבא's question from step 8. The heater did not cause the wood to become חולין, so רב חסדא's ruling that the bread is forbidden still stands.

phrases.english: When done intentionally, what is the reason it does not [become non-holy]?
Since it is not subject to misuse-of-holy-property law,
it does not go out to non-holy status.
Peace-offerings as well:
since they are not subject to misuse-of-holy-property law,
phrases.notes: Before the blood is sprinkled, שלמים are not subject to מעילה.

phrases.english: it does not go out to non-holy status.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רב פפא's answer in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the reason behind the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any use of הקדש, even on purpose, takes the wood out to חולין.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only use that is subject to מעילה frees הקדש. שלמים wood is not subject to it, so it stays forbidden.

steps.title: Does misuse really make the wood non-holy? A ברייתא says holy ash is always forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that מעילה turns the wood into חולין. A ברייתא teaches that אפר הקדש is forbidden forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it true that whenever the person heating the oven commits מעילה, the wood becomes חולין? But a ברייתא teaches: the ash of anything that must be burned is permitted, except the wood of an אשירה. And אפר הקדש is always forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the basic assumption behind רבא's question in step 8, that מעילה frees the wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If מעילה made the wood חולין, the ash left over should be permitted. The ברייתא says אפר הקדש stays forbidden forever. That suggests burning or misusing הקדש does not free it.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who heats or fires up the oven
Forbidden items that must be burned
A tree used for idol worship

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge targets רבא's general rule, that מעילה frees הקדש. It is not a challenge to רב פפא's answer about שלמים.

phrases.english: And wherever the one who heats [the oven] commits misuse,
does it go out to non-holy status?
But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא:
All items that are burned, their ash is permitted,
except for the wood of an asheira.
And holy-property ash is forbidden forever.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back and questions the premise of רבא's question.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's premise that מעילה turns הקדש wood into חולין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says אפר הקדש is always forbidden, which suggests that burning or misusing it does not free it.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: the ברייתא is about a fire that started by itself
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא speaks of הקדש wood that caught fire on its own. Nobody committed מעילה, so the ash stays holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: the case is where a fire broke out by itself in הקדש wood, so there was no person who committed מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא answers the challenge by narrowing the case of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעילה needs a person who misuses the הקדש. When a fire starts by itself, there is no מעילה, so nothing frees the wood and the ash stays forbidden. When a person does commit מעילה, the wood does become חולין, so רבא's premise survives.

keyTerms.meaning: A fire that started by itself

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said:
For example, where a fire broke out by itself
among holy-property wood,
so there is no person who committed misuse.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא כְּגוֹן שֶׁנָּפְלָה דְּלֵיקָה מֵאֵילֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means all אפר הקדש stays forbidden, even after מעילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only about a case with no מעילה, such as a fire that started by itself.

steps.title: רב שמעיה: the ברייתא is about holy ash that must be buried
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא refers to ash that requires גניזה, like the ash taken from the מזבח. Burning it was part of the עבודה, so there was no מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמעיה said: the ברייתא is about ash that must be put away and buried. As a ברייתא teaches about the פסוק "וְשָׂמוֹ" ("and he shall put it"): put it down gently, put all of it, and do not scatter it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמעיה gives a second, different answer to the same challenge, and supports it with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ash from the מזבח was burned as part of the קרבן's proper עבודה, so no מעילה happened. The פסוק "ושמו" shows that this ash keeps its holiness and must be handled with care. So the ברייתא is not talking about ordinary הקדש wood misused by a person.

keyTerms.meaning: Putting away or burying holy items
That he should not scatter it

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers explain why אפר הקדש stays forbidden. רמי בר חמא: nobody committed מעילה. רב שמעיה: the ash is the kind that must be buried, and it was burned as a מצוה. Either way, a person's מעילה still makes הקדש into חולין.

phrases.english: Rav Shemaya said:
[It refers] to those that require burial.
As it was taught in a ברייתא:
"And he shall put it": gently;
"and he shall put it": all of it;
"and he shall put it": that he not scatter it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שְׁמַעְיָה אָמַר בְּאוֹתָן שֶׁטְּעוּנִין גְּנִיזָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 11, different from רמי בר חמא's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a different category of ash
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about all הקדש ash.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about ash that requires גניזה, which was burned as part of a מצוה with no מעילה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מעילה by a person still frees הקדש. The ברייתא's ash stays forbidden for a separate reason.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי יהודה says חמץ must be burned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה says the only way to destroy חמץ is by burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי יהודה says there is no destroying [חמץ] except by burning. A ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה said, the destruction of חמץ is only by burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of הקדש and opens a new section on רבי יהודה's view in the משנה. This step sets up his proof, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא discussed benefit from forbidden items, such as bread baked with ערלה or הקדש wood. Now it starts analyzing the משנה's argument about how חמץ must be destroyed. The ברייתא repeats רבי יהודה's position so that his reasoning can follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Destroying or getting rid of חמץ

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר אֵין בִּיעוּר וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: [The משנה said:] Rabbi Yehuda says: there is no removal, etc.
It was taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Yehuda said:
the removal of leavened bread is only by burning,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, חמץ may only be destroyed by burning.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's קל וחומר from נותר
steps.stepSummary: נותר is a lighter case, since it has no בל יראה. It still must be burned. So חמץ, which is stricter, must certainly be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And logic supports this. נותר is not under the prohibitions of בל יראה and בל ימצא, and it still must be burned. חמץ is under בל יראה and בל ימצא, so surely it must be burned!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה proves his position with a קל וחומר from נותר (leftover קרבן meat).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument has two steps. First, נותר is the more lenient case, and the Torah still requires it to be burned. Second, חמץ is stricter because it carries the extra prohibitions of בל יראה and בל ימצא. So it must certainly be burned as well.

keyTerms.meaning: קרבן meat left past its time limit
The bans on חמץ being seen or found in one's possession

phrases.english: And logic dictates:
Just as leftover sacrificial meat,
which is not under "it shall not be seen" and "it shall not be found,"
requires burning,

phrases.aramaic: חָמֵץ שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ בְּ״בַל יֵרָאֶה״ וּ״בַל יִמָּצֵא״ —
phrases.english: leavened bread, which is under "it shall not be seen" and "it shall not be found,"
is it not all the more so that it requires burning!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the logical proof for the ruling quoted in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's rule that ביעור חמץ is only by burning
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from נותר, which must be burned even though it has no בל יראה

steps.title: The חכמים reject the קל וחומר because it ends up lenient
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say that an argument which starts strict and ends lenient is not valid. If burning is the only way, a person with no wood could never destroy his חמץ. But the Torah wants it destroyed any way possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Any argument that starts out strict and ends up lenient is not a real argument. If someone has no wood to burn his חמץ, should he just sit and do nothing? But the Torah said, 'Destroy leaven from your houses,' meaning in any way you are able to destroy it!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים knock down the קל וחומר that רבי יהודה made from נותר in step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה wanted to be strict by requiring burning only. The חכמים show the hidden leniency: with no wood available, the person would have no way to fulfill תשביתו at all. The word תשביתו means destroying it by any means, so limiting it to burning actually weakens the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument used to derive a law (here, the קל וחומר)
'You shall destroy / remove,' the Torah's command to get rid of חמץ

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are not saying burning is forbidden. They are saying burning cannot be the ONLY way. Any method of destroying חמץ works.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: כׇּל דִּין שֶׁאַתָּה דָּן
phrases.english: They said to him: Any logical argument that you argue
phrases.notes: 'They' are the חכמים, answering רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: whose beginning is to be strict and whose end is to be lenient
is not a valid argument.
If he did not find wood to burn it,
should he sit idle and do nothing?
phrases.notes: This is the leniency hidden inside רבי יהודה's strict rule.

phrases.english: But the Torah said: 'You shall destroy leaven from your houses,'
meaning with anything by which you are able to destroy it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: כׇּל דִּין שֶׁאַתָּה דָּן תְּחִלָּתוֹ לְהַחְמִיר וְסוֹפוֹ לְהָקֵל אֵינוֹ דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר from נותר presented in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire קל וחומר that requires burning only.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The argument leads to a leniency: with no wood, there would be no way to destroy the חמץ, which goes against the meaning of תשביתו.

steps.title: רבי יהודה compares חמץ to נותר because both are forbidden to eat
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה offers a new argument. נותר and חמץ are both forbidden to eat. Since נותר is burned, חמץ should be burned too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה came back and made a different argument: נותר is forbidden to eat, and חמץ is forbidden to eat. Just as נותר is burned, so too חמץ is burned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה drops the קל וחומר and tries a new kind of proof: a direct comparison between נותר and חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time he does not argue 'how much more so.' He argues 'they are alike.' He claims that a shared feature (being forbidden to eat) means they share the same method of destruction (burning).

keyTerms.meaning: He went back and argued a different argument
Just as ... so too (the formula for a comparison)

phrases.aramaic: חָזַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְדָנוֹ דִּין אַחֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda went back and argued a different argument:
Leftover sacrificial meat is forbidden to eat,
and leavened bread is forbidden to eat.
Just as leftover sacrificial meat is destroyed by burning,
so too leavened bread is destroyed by burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְדָנוֹ דִּין אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the קל וחומר is rejected, רבי יהודה offers a new comparison-based proof.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's ruling that חמץ must be burned.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A comparison to נותר, based on the shared feature of being forbidden to eat.

steps.title: The חכמים point to נבילה, which is forbidden to eat but not burned
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that נבילה proves the comparison wrong. It is forbidden to eat, yet it does not need to be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: נבילה will prove otherwise. It is forbidden to eat, yet it does not need burning!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give a counter-example that breaks רבי יהודה's comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being forbidden to eat were enough to require burning, נבילה would also have to be burned. Since it does not, the feature רבי יהודה chose cannot be the reason נותר is burned.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה

phrases.english: They said to him: An animal carcass will prove otherwise,
since it is forbidden to eat
and yet it does not require burning!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison from step 17 with a counter-example.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison based only on being forbidden to eat.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: נבילה shares that feature but is not burned, so the feature does not explain burning.

steps.title: רבי יהודה adds that both are also forbidden for benefit
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה points out a difference. נבילה may be used for benefit, but נותר and חמץ are forbidden both to eat and for benefit. So חמץ should be burned like נותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: There is a difference. נותר is forbidden to eat and to benefit from, and חמץ is forbidden to eat and to benefit from. Just as נותר needs burning, so too חמץ needs burning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה defends his comparison by adding a second shared feature that נבילה does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבילה is only forbidden to eat. A person may still benefit from it, for example by selling it to a נכרי. By adding איסור הנאה, רבי יהודה makes the comparison tighter, so נבילה no longer fits.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference (between the cases)
Forbidden to benefit from in any way

phrases.english: He said to them: There is a difference:
leftover sacrificial meat is forbidden to eat and to benefit from,
and leavened bread is forbidden to eat and to benefit from.
phrases.notes: נבילה, by contrast, is permitted for benefit.

phrases.english: Just as leftover sacrificial meat requires burning,
so too leavened bread requires burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the נבילה counter-example by narrowing the comparison.
steps.raayaSupportSource: נותר, now matched on two features: forbidden to eat and forbidden for benefit.

steps.title: The חכמים point to שור הנסקל, which is forbidden to eat and for benefit but not burned
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים bring a new counter-example. A שור הנסקל is forbidden both to eat and for benefit, yet it does not need burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: A stoned ox will prove otherwise. It is forbidden to eat and to benefit from, yet it does not need burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים find a case that matches both of רבי יהודה's features but is still not burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ox that killed a person is stoned, and its meat is then forbidden to eat and for benefit. It matches the new two-part comparison, yet it is buried, not burned. So even these two features do not explain why נותר is burned.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox stoned to death by בית דין for killing a person

phrases.english: They said to him: An ox that is stoned will prove otherwise,
since it is forbidden to eat and to benefit from,
and yet it does not require burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the refined comparison from step 19 with a new counter-example.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison based on being forbidden to eat and for benefit.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שור הנסקל shares both features but is not burned.

steps.title: רבי יהודה adds that both also carry the punishment of כרת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה adds a third feature. Both נותר and חמץ carry כרת, but eating a שור הנסקל does not. So חמץ should be burned like נותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: There is a difference. נותר is forbidden to eat and to benefit from, and one who eats it is punished with כרת. חמץ is forbidden to eat and to benefit from, and one who eats it is punished with כרת. Just as נותר is burned, so too חמץ is burned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה narrows his comparison again, this time adding the severe punishment of כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating a שור הנסקל is a regular prohibition without כרת. Now נותר and חמץ share three features that the ox lacks, so רבי יהודה says the counter-example fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Spiritual cutting off, a severe heavenly punishment

phrases.english: He said to them: There is a difference:
leftover sacrificial meat is forbidden to eat and to benefit from
and is punished with כרת,
and leavened bread is forbidden to eat and to benefit from
and is punished with כרת,
phrases.notes: Eating a stoned ox does not carry כרת.

phrases.english: just as leftover sacrificial meat is destroyed by burning,
so too leavened bread is destroyed by burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שור הנסקל counter-example by adding the feature of כרת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: נותר, now matched on three features: forbidden to eat, forbidden for benefit, and punished with כרת.

steps.title: The חכמים point to the חלב of a שור הנסקל, which has all three features but is not burned
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים bring the fats of a שור הנסקל. They are forbidden to eat and for benefit, eating them carries כרת, and yet they do not need burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: The forbidden fat of a stoned ox will prove otherwise. It is forbidden to eat and to benefit from, and one who eats it is punished with כרת, yet it does not need burning!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים find a case that matches all three of רבי יהודה's features and still is not burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ox's חלב carries כרת because eating חלב always carries כרת. It is also forbidden for benefit because it comes from a שור הנסקל. It matches every feature of the comparison, yet it is not burned, so רבי יהודה's comparison fails again.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden animal fats, which carry כרת if eaten

steps.confusionAlert: The כרת here comes from the general איסור of חלב, not from the ox being stoned. The איסור הנאה comes from the stoning. Together, the חלב has all three features.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the pattern of a 'מה מצינו' comparison. Each time a counter-example appears, the one making the comparison must find a feature that separates his case, or the comparison collapses.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: חֶלְבּוֹ שֶׁל שׁוֹר הַנִּסְקָל יוֹכִיחַ,
phrases.english: They said to him: The forbidden fat of a stoned ox will prove otherwise,
since it is forbidden to eat and to benefit from
and one is punished with כרת for eating it,
and yet it does not require burning!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: חֶלְבּוֹ שֶׁל שׁוֹר הַנִּסְקָל יוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the three-feature comparison from step 21 with a counter-example that has all three features.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison based on איסור אכילה, איסור הנאה, and כרת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The חלב of a שור הנסקל has all three features but is not burned.
